macro.overnight_read: The market is fragmenting heavily along inflation lines: crude oil climbing above $102 is driving strong bids into energy (USO +3.63%, XLE +3.06%), while crushing airlines and transport names. Mega-cap tech sentiment is rattled by Meta's Q3 free cash flow swinging to negative $2.12B on heavy AI capex, leaving crowded Nasdaq positioning (97th percentile) vulnerable to further de-risking.
macro.summary: We are operating in a defensive, stagflationary-tilted tape with crude oil topping $102 and the 10-year Treasury yield sticky at 5.13%. Capital is fleeing capital-intensive tech (SMH -12.52% over 20 days) and rotating into cash-flow havens like energy (XLE +12.24% over 20 days) and consumer staples. Our strategy today is to ride long energy and defensive momentum while aggressively shorting fuel-impacted airlines and fading crowded tech bounces. With the FOMC rate decision next Wednesday and VIX hovering at 19.19, maintain tight stops and trim risk into Friday's close.
